notes: Hancock treats contemporary rock and R&B material as modern jazz repertoire rather than as novelty covers.
The core group includes Herbie Hancock, Michael Brecker, John Scofield, Dave Holland, Jack DeJohnette and Don Alias; selected tracks add strings and woodwinds/brass.
A solo-guitar album of songs written by others, and Metheny's first album without his own compositions.
The record uses several guitar configurations, including baritone, 42-string, 6-string and nylon-string guitars.

tracks.title: That's the Way I've Always Heard It Should Be

notes: A live solo-piano set built around ten Beatles songs, followed by David Bowie’s “Life on Mars?” as a bridge to later pop songwriting.
Recorded at Philharmonie de Paris in September 2020.
Ryan Adams re-recorded Taylor Swift’s 1989 song-for-song, shifting the material toward a looser singer-songwriter and rock palette.
The album was produced by Ryan Adams and Charlie Stavish.

tracks.title: All You Had to Do Was Stay

notes: Ten Bon Scott-era AC/DC songs are stripped down and substantially rearranged rather than reproduced as hard-rock covers.
The record is a useful example of how dramatically familiar material can change when arrangement and scale are reduced.

tracks.title: Up to My Neck in You
You Ain't Got a Hold on Me

notes: Hynde and James Walbourne assembled the Dylan set remotely during lockdown, building arrangements by sending ideas and recordings back and forth.
The nine-song collection stays focused on Dylan rather than mixing the tribute with unrelated material.

tracks.title: Don't Fall Apart on Me Tonight

notes: The first Lu’s Jukebox set is a Tom Petty tribute drawn from across his catalog and performed as a full-band studio concert.
The closing track, “Stolen Moments,” is a Lucinda Williams original rather than a Petty cover.
